account: Paige.AI of New York submitted Paige Prostate, software that flags the spot on a digitized prostate needle biopsy slide most likely to hold cancer. In the pivotal reader study, sixteen pathologists read each whole slide image first without the software and then with its result. FDA reviewers report that for 171 slides with cancer, the net change toward a cancer or defer call gave an improvement in sensitivity in 7.3% of biopsy images. Specificity rose from 88.45% to 89.50%. FDA granted the De Novo request on 21 September 2021. The reviewers write that the analysis is per biopsy and that the benefit per patient would likely be lower than 7.3%, because patients usually have several core biopsies and many have cancer in more than one. The reads were made in a study setting and did not guide care.

ai_role.statement: Each pathologist read every image unassisted and then assisted, so the change in calls is attributed to the software result.
